headline: Decoder says Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO; Anthropic IPO called days away

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's twenty to four UTC on Friday, November thirteenth. This is ARA AI News. Decoder is claiming a leadership break at Nvidia, and that is the change since our last bulletin.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Decoder says it rewrote its intro minutes before publishing because Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive, as the affair reports and the alleged Chinese-spy claims threatened to take over the company.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: We do not have an Nvidia statement, a board filing, or a named successor in this hour. The A I Daily Brief's headlines listed spy-scandal fallout and did not say Huang was out.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Decoder's notes call it an emergency intro update and say they will have more as it develops. The rest of that episode is a foreign-policy conversation with Kyle Chan from two days earlier, not a first-party Nvidia interview.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The board already had this story from Hard Fork. That show cited Times reporting that Huang admitted an affair with Megaspeed's Alice Huang, alleged by United States officials to be a Chinese spy.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Hard Fork guests also described a Malaysia preferred-cloud partner in twenty twenty-three. They said if ten or fifteen percent of Nvidia's revenue was coming from Malaysia, those chips were being distributed to China in one way or another.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Those remain allegations, not a company admission. Last night on twenty VC, guests said hosting inference and G P U chips for China-based models in Singapore and Thailand is a problem even beyond the spy case.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: They argued that selling those chips into China and hosting them just across the border will all get shut down. They said a measure had already passed the House and then stalled in the Senate.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The other fresh notes this hour are on Anthropic. The A I Daily Brief says the I P O is days away, and that Wall Street still does not know how to price the company.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The show says it walks through a share-price range, shifting valuation chatter, compute commitments, and a new Claude productivity suite aimed at Microsoft. We do not have those figures, because this item is also show notes only.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That is new color, not a filing. Last night on twenty VC, a guest still framed one point four trillion dollars versus one trillion as options on the private side, with per-share value up about twenty to thirty percent.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That same guest said a trillion-dollar allocator was not worried about this eighty billion dollars, but about the next hundred billion, because that layer is very thin. Kalshi's December I P O odds had already fallen from nearly ninety percent to fifty-seven.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The Wall Street Journal's skepticism of a one point five trillion dollar number, and that November nineteenth call at one point three trillion, still stand. Watch Anthropic for a filing or a roadshow in the next few days, and whether that Claude suite for Microsoft is a real product.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Watch Nvidia first. We need the company on the record, a successor, or a filing that names the handover, because until then the live fact is Decoder's claim sitting on top of the Hard Fork affair reporting and the twenty VC export warning.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's ARA AI News. We'll be back when the picture changes.
